name: Air Fryer Coconut Shrimp with Rice and Apricot Dipping Sauce

components.name: Coconut Shrimp

ingredients.name: Raw peeled and deveined large shrimp, tail off
Plain flour for coating, whole batch weighed
Raw whole egg, beaten without shell

steps: Dry the raw shrimp thoroughly. Dip each shrimp in flour, then egg, then coconut-panko mixture; press crumbs to adhere. Discard dredges left over after touching raw seafood.
Spray shrimp with measured oil. Air fry at 190 C for 5-7 minutes in small batches, turning halfway, until shrimp reach 63 C and crust is golden.
Pack a quarter of coconut shrimp and cooked rice in each container; package sauce and cucumber separately. Reheat shrimp in air fryer, not microwave, where possible.

components.name: Jasmine Rice
steps: Cook rice with measured water and keep warm or cool quickly for storage. Combine coconut flakes, panko and salt in one bowl, flour in another, and beaten egg in a third.

components.name: Apricot Sauce & Cucumber

ingredients.name: Raw cucumber, sliced for cold side

steps: Mix apricot preserves with rice vinegar and chilli flakes to make the dipping sauce; if too thick, gently warm to combine and cool before packing.
Slice fresh cucumber and add lime juice just before serving to maintain crunch.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.

Skinnytaste coconut shrimp and apricot sauce support air-fryer method. UNHANGRY formulation increases shrimp to a complete main and adds rice and cucumber. Flour/egg unused after dredging means calculated macros may be overstated.
Planning: SECONDARY STOVETOP rice; batch-frying increases active time.
Freezer: breaded shrimp can be frozen but lose crispness; rice freezes quickly cooled; cucumber NOT freezer-friendly

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Shrimp — plan for days 1-3; the cucumber side doesn't freeze.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; for many fish and shrimp dishes, prioritize eating within 1-2 days for quality and freeze later-week cooked portions promptly.

Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard, and reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. For crab cakes containing egg binder and purchased cooked crab, reheat to 74 C.
When recipe includes rice, cool rapidly and refrigerate promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Re-crisp breading in an air fryer when possible.
Do not freeze fresh avocado, uncooked tomato/cucumber/cabbage salad, or mayonnaise/yogurt-based dressing unless kitchen-tested separately.
